came_from: Owner orders for the 6.4.0 SCITT anchor, in work packages: the first package (fetch and recompute real CCF receipts offline, ADR 0009), AP2 to AP4 (a `scitt-ccf/v1` reader behind the optional `[scitt]` extra, the statement signature, receipt verification under `rp_trust`), the owner answers Q1 to Q8, N1 to N7, S1 and S2, a measurement of section 4 of draft-ietf-scitt-receipts-ccf-profile-05 for its focused working group last call, and a differential corpus of one-variable mutations registered on a local scitt-ccf-ledger. After this pull request was opened: five Codex rounds and their fixes, the owner decisions A1 (keys built by their own type) and A2 (the measuring tools named in the key sweep), a CodeQL finding on a test key, and the owner order of 2026-09-26 to identify the exact preimage of the receipt's data-hash and then add four further mutation classes.
change:
A new optional module, `proofbundle.scitt_ccf`, reads a SCITT Transparent Statement with CCF receipts under the narrow profile of ADR 0009. It needs the `[scitt]` extra (`cbor2==6.1.4`); without it every entry point refuses with `no_lib` and nothing falls back. A structural pre-scan of its own (`proofbundle._cbor_prescan`) runs before cbor2 sees any byte: definite lengths, shortest heads, no floats, unique map keys, tag 18 only at the top and tag 1 only around an integer CWT time claim.

Three public verifiers, none of them registered as an anchor type and none reachable from any verify path: `verify_statement_signature`, `verify_transparent_statement` and `verify_consistency_receipt`. The statement key is selected by the protected `x5chain` and never trusted from it; a statement without one is outside the profile. Consistency receipts have their own closed status set, and two forms the section 4.2 pseudo-code accepts are refused because sections 4 and 4.1 say MUST: a corrupted second proof, and an anchor below the one section 4 requires.

`tools/scitt_ccf_external/` holds the measuring tools and their recorded runs: the fetch of third-party bytes at pinned commits, the recomputation, the local-ledger probes, the comparison with microsoft/scitt-verifier, the section 4 measurement with its findings for the working group in `SECTION4_WGLC.md`, and the differential corpus as raw hex text with views derived by the tool.

The reader builds a key only by its own type (owner decision A1): EC P-256 and P-384 from the encoded point, RSA from its numbers, and every other key type refused before any key object exists, the x5chain end-entity key read from the TBS SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

`tools/scitt_ccf_external/preimage_candidates.py` computes ten candidates for the preimage of the data-hash per accepted corpus vector, and `differential_corpus_round2/` is a second corpus round in four classes: protected-header encodings and orderings, duplicate and both-bucket labels, crit, and the control's bytes after a configuration change and after a service recovery. One byte string is the preimage in every accepted vector of both rounds: tag 18, a definite four-element array, the protected, payload and signature byte strings with preferred heads and the protected content as sent, and an empty unprotected map. It is the byte string the service source builds (scitt-ccf-ledger `app/src/main.cpp` lines 417 to 425, CCF 7.0.17 `src/crypto/cose.cpp` lines 18 to 89, read, not run).
fix: The reader is an optional module and not a change to an existing verify path, so every bundle and every existing verdict is untouched until AP5 registers the anchor type. Outside `src/`, `tests/` and `tools/scitt_ccf_external/`, the branch changes four files on purpose: `pyproject.toml` (the `[scitt]` extra, the same pin in `dev`, and the mypy file count 72 to 74), `scripts/rust_parity_registry.json` (three `PENDING` entries, owner answer N5 a), `scripts/type_confusion_gate.py` (benign `older_root` and `older_issuer` fixtures, so the gate evaluates the new surface instead of stopping at `NEEDS_FIXTURE`), and `docs/adr/0009-scitt-anchor-cose-profile.md`.

not_changed:
No verify path, no verdict and no exit code of an existing surface: the three new verifiers are reachable only by calling them. `tools/pb_verify_rs`, `.github/`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the version number are untouched, and Rust parity for the new surfaces stays `PENDING` until AP5.

Known limits. Every service measured ran locally in virtual mode, with no TEE, on one node; no production service was measured, and no service measured emits a consistency receipt, so the section 4 receipt is the service's own signature over the newer root with a proof computed from the ledger's leaves. The last-call mail, the datatracker page, the rendered draft and the published RFC texts were not reachable from the agent's environment; the working group sources at pinned commits were read instead. The two full-suite failures are measured as a root-only effect of that environment. The full suite on the tree merged with the current main was not run; `git merge-tree` against main `8a6594be` reports a conflict in `pyproject.toml`, the mypy file count, which a trial merge resolves at 75 files with mypy 2.3.0 clean. A software-version boundary of the service is NOT MEASURABLE here: one service image, no network.

AGENTS.md line 21 says no network in the agent phase; the first measurement orders needed git clones of third-party repositories and a local ledger build, so that line is not met for those sessions. The second corpus round used the image already built and no network. The corpora are text, 467305 and 353362 bytes; whether that is large under the same line is left to the maintainer. The commits are unsigned under the maintainer's author identity (owner answer N6 a). The findings for the working group in `SECTION4_WGLC.md` are measurements and questions, not a position of the project.
